---
title: "Greedy Decoding"
description: "A generation strategy that selects the highest-scoring next token at each step."
term: "Greedy Decoding"
letter: "G"
category: "LLM Engineering"
difficulty: "Intermediate"
---

## Simple explanation

Greedy decoding generates a sequence one token at a time, choosing the
most likely next token at each step. It is simple and fast, but an
early choice can lead to a less desirable complete sequence.

## Technical explanation

At each step $t$, greedy decoding selects
$x_t=\arg\max_x p(x\mid x_{<t})$. The chosen token is appended to the
prefix, and the model predicts again until a stopping condition. It
does not search over all possible sequences and is not guaranteed to
maximize the probability of the entire sequence.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Greedy decoding provides a deterministic baseline for generation when
model outputs are stable. Its speed and reproducibility may be useful,
but output quality depends on the task and model distribution.

## How it works

The model produces next-token scores or probabilities, the decoder
chooses the highest-scoring token, and generation repeats. Special
stopping tokens, maximum lengths, and constraints affect when decoding
ends.

## Practical example

A language model asked to complete a short factual phrase can repeatedly
choose its highest-probability next token until it produces a stop
token or reaches the output limit.

## Common misconceptions

- Greedy decoding is not equivalent to exhaustive search.
- Choosing the best token at every step does not ensure the best
  complete sequence.
- Deterministic decoding does not guarantee factual or repeatable
  results if other parts of the system are nondeterministic.
